title: Fynaptix · AI & Compute Research
heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (~$190B CY2026 / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027) — combined $825–855B, unchanged: no hyperscaler has reported since the last edition and the big-four prints land in late October. Debt funding still sits near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). The RBA's Oct 1 estimate of US$1–1.5 trillion in off-balance-sheet and vendor-financed obligations (20–30 year debt against hardware of 'uncertain economic lives') remains the sharpest official warning; the 10-year Treasury touched ~5.37% on Oct 8, a 24-year high, before easing to ~5.25%

kpis.sub: OPENAI'S REVENUE RESET VS. ANTHROPIC'S NOVEMBER IPO
kpis.label: The Financial Times reported Oct 8 that OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50B at end-September, not the ~$70B widely reported — a definitional gap (investors had grossed OpenAI up to compare with Anthropic's cloud-partner-inclusive accounting) rather than lost sales, but it hit AI stocks anyway (Nasdaq −1.3%, SOXX −3.5%, Oracle −5%+). Bloomberg followed Oct 9 that OpenAI still expects ~$70B annualized by year-end. Its pending $30B+ round at a reported $1.4T pre-money is now ~28x the lower figure (vs. 20x); Altman has ruled out a 2026 IPO and Polymarket odds of a 2027 listing fell to ~58% from ~80%. Anthropic's leaked S-1 (SiliconANGLE, Sept 29) shows revenue of $4.6B in 2025 (from ~$0.4B), $11.5B in Q2 2026 alone (FT), a $42B 2025 net loss ($8B operating loss, >91% compute), and $518B of compute commitments ~80% of which are non-cancellable; IPO reportedly November, up to $100B raised, at $2T+ (some reports $2.3T) — all subject to change

kpis.sub: BIS: SHARE OF AI INVESTMENT THAT IS AI-TO-AI; H1 2026 GLOBAL VC
kpis.label: The BIS (Bulletin 137, Oct 1) found that 55.2% of investment value flowing into 1,246 AI-supply-chain firms (2021–2025) came from other AI firms, and 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value involved supply-chain relationships — the first central-bank quantification of circular financing, though the RBA noted aggregate leverage remains contained. This week added fresh examples: Broadcom is reportedly arranging $50B+ of financing for custom chips developed with OpenAI (WSJ), and Anthropic's S-1 lists ~$161B of Broadcom equipment-lease contracts. H1 2026 global venture funding hit a record $510B (Crunchbase) with AI taking an estimated 70–80%, and corporate investors account for ~88% of US AI venture deal value (PitchBook) with Nvidia the largest single corporate investor

kpis.sub: NVIDIA: RECORD HIGH OCT 6, THEN THE OPENAI REVENUE SCARE
kpis.label: Nvidia hit an intraday record of $243.37 on Oct 6, fell ~3% to ~$230 on Oct 8 (worst Dow component) when the FT's OpenAI revenue report hit, and bounced ~2% Oct 9 after TSMC's record September sales and a Cantor note that Micron's HBM supply/pricing is intact. Stock is ~+25–28% YTD (from a ~$164 March low) at ~29x forward earnings by one count (other sources cite 16–17x on FY2028 estimates — multiples vary by horizon). Q2 FY27 revenue was $96.2B (+106%, Data Center $89.0B) at ~75% gross margin; Q3 guide is ~$108B ±2% (~+89%, a slowing rate of growth), and the $150B buyback increase (authorized Sept 28) leaves ~$235B through fiscal 2028. Bulls see a cheap compounder; bears see a company financing its customers (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI) while buying back its own stock — Burry's Oct 2 1960s computer-leasing analogy still stands. Q3 FY27 results are expected in November

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit (up from Sequoia's $200B framing in late 2023), while AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year. This week's FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is ~$50B, not ~$70B, sharpened the point: the largest buyer of compute has a smaller revenue base than the market assumed, and the Nasdaq fell 1.3% on the day. Counterpoint: the gap is largely accounting (net vs. gross of cloud-partner sales), Anthropic's Q2 revenue of $11.5B and its reported move to adjusted operating profit show real demand, and Bloomberg reports OpenAI still expects ~$70B by year-end. The BIS's June 2026 annual report still names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks.

bear_case.title: AI's own architects sound the alarm
bear_case.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier" on Sept 12, arguing AI capability growth has accelerated "drastically faster" since summer 2026 — driven mainly by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI — and proposing independent safety evaluation, inter-lab coordination and international cooperation. OpenAI's Sam Altman and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis publicly backed the call; days later Palantir's Alex Karp went further, telling CNBC that frontier labs may need to be nationalized over "unlimited risk." The market reaction was real — chip names sold off while Meta, Alphabet and Microsoft rose — but skeptics note that a company mid-prep for a ~$2T IPO calling for the industry to slow down is also a moat-building and regulatory-capture argument, not purely an act of altruism.

bear_case.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism — but strength can still win the argument
bear_case.description: The 10-year Treasury touched ~5.37% on Oct 8 — its highest in 24 years — before easing to ~5.25%, with oil near $90 WTI / $104 Brent adding inflation pressure and consumer sentiment at a five-month low (46.3). BofA estimates AI-related corporate debt sales have added roughly 0.3 percentage points to 10-year rates this year, and Nomura pegs hyperscaler borrowing at ~25% of net Treasury note/bond issuance to private investors. Counterpoint: the S&P 500 (7,811) is near its all-time high, all three major indexes finished the week higher, and TSMC's record September sales suggest physical demand is intact.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments off hyperscaler balance sheets, and the RBA's Oct 1 Financial Stability Review put hyperscaler obligations via SPVs and vendor financing at US$1–1.5T, financed with 20–30 year debt against hardware of 'uncertain economic lives'. Anthropic's leaked S-1 adds a lab-level data point: $518B of compute commitments, ~80% non-cancellable or take-or-pay. The RBA also noted aggregate leverage remains contained. Oracle remains the starkest case (BBB-, FY26 FCF −$23.7B, S&P ~$42B FY27 deficit) and fell 5%+ on Oct 8.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: The BIS (Bulletin 137, Oct 1) found 55.2% of investment value into 1,246 AI-supply-chain firms came from other AI firms, 28.7% of AI firms' invested value went to other AI firms, and 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value involved supply-chain relationships. New this week: Broadcom is reportedly arranging $50B+ of financing for OpenAI's custom chips, Anthropic's S-1 shows ~$161B of Broadcom equipment-lease contracts, and Nvidia is in talks to anchor up to $10B of Anthropic's IPO. Burry calls Nvidia's revenue 'majority circularly financed'. Counterpoint: the BIS frames this as a feature of a young supply chain rather than proof of systemic risk, and Anthropic's reported path to adjusted operating profit suggests at least one lab can fund itself.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; Burry argues replacement cycles are really 2–3 years, understating depreciation by ~$176B across 2026–2028 and inflating Oracle's earnings by ~27% and Meta's by ~21%. On Sept 27 Nvidia published data arguing A100/H100/B200 hardware retains value beyond accelerated depreciation schedules, and on Oct 2 Burry replied by citing the 1960s computer-leasing bubble ('The Money Game'). Bull evidence: CoreWeave's CEO says H100 capacity was rebooked at ~95% of the original contract price and Nvidia says A100s are rented through 2029 — nine years after launch. Bear evidence: that is rental pricing for the best-contracted capacity, not proof the economic life of the whole installed base is 5–6 years.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Layoffs.fyi's tracker showed 128,536 tech workers cut across 299 companies in 2026 through Sept 10 (not refreshed this edition) — already exceeding all of 2025 — while a broader tracker (SkillSyncer, different methodology) counts 210,741 workers across 383 layoff events through Sept 20. xAI itself cut roughly 500 data-annotation staff (a third of that team) on Sept 12 as part of a stated pivot to "specialist AI tutors." The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, record layoffs, and AI labs restructuring their own workforces — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean partly on cost-cutting elsewhere, not purely on AI revenue.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took over 40% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total, and AI took 86% of all US venture dollars in H1 per PitchBook), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. NVIDIA now sits at the center of deals spanning chips (TSMC, Broadcom), model hosting (Hugging Face), enterprise software (Palantir) and a potential anchor stake in Anthropic's IPO — a single company's balance sheet increasingly touches nearly every layer of this page, even as customers like Anthropic simultaneously build Google TPU alternatives. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters and Oracle's Sept 10 beat is a live example — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.
